_comment: SNAPSHOT of every COORDINATOR_OVERRIDE_/ALLOW_/SCOPE_ variable the Bash|PowerShell PreToolUse chain can consult, as of the type:"http" flip (C7, 2026-08-29). WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: on the http transport a caller's environment reaches the guard ONLY through registration headers -- allowedEnvVars interpolates into headers and nothing else, and the POST body carries no env key under any spelling. There is no wildcard: each variable needs its own X-Coordinator-Env-<NAME> header in hooks.json. A variable missing from that header set does not error -- the override is simply never seen, and the guard denies as though the operator had asked for nothing. That is the restrictive direction, not fail-open, but it is silent, which is why it gets a pinned snapshot rather than a comment. test_forwardable_env_headers_cover_every_override_var compares hooks.json against this list, so a var added here without its header fails loudly instead of degrading quietly. When a guard gains a new override variable, add it here AND to the registration's headers/allowedEnvVars in the same commit. The list is a SNAPSHOT, not a live derivation: deriving it would mean reading claude-klabauter's tree from this repo's tests, which would make the fast tier depend on a sibling clone being present.
